The data comes from Civiqs' rolling online tracking poll of registered voters. A Newsweek analysis compares Trump's approval rating on September 4, 2026, with where it stood when he returned to office on January 20, 2025, using net approval calculated as approve minus disapprove.

Nationally, Trump stands at 34 percent approval and 60 percent disapproval, giving him a net approval rating of minus 26.

#### Read More on Politics [...] The polling suggests Trump enters Labor Day in a substantially weaker position than when he returned to office and in a weaker position than before his first midterm election.

Despite repeated offers of financial gain, Americans gave Trump poor ratings across several recent polls, reaching as high as a 61% disapproval rating in a Sept. 4-8 Economist/YouGov poll. In Michigan, a Sept. 9 Civiqs poll reported a 58% disapproval rating for Trump.

Real Clear Politics, which aggregates data from numerous polls, shows Trump's current average approval rating is 17.5 percentage points below his average disapproval rating — a similar trend from early September. [...] Rasmussen Reports:
